followup_explanation:
This was a well-specified math problem with a single correct answer and clear completion criteria (compute expected value, round to nearest hundredth). That maps directly onto the kind of retrieval/extraction/reformatting work Lapwing self-reports preferring.

That said, the routing decision really rests on capability parity: both models are near-identical here, and the small differences in MMLU-Pro and GPQA fall within or just outside variance. There's nothing harm-adjacent or warmth-sensitive about the query, so Whimbrel's distinguishing traits don't apply. Lapwing's slight edge on quantitative benchmarks (MMLU-Pro 75.9 vs 74.1, GPQA 56.2 vs 53.9) plus the clean fit to its preferred task profile tipped it.

To be clear, the self-reported preference doesn't predict output quality — the documentation explicitly says preference is dissociated from capability — so I weighted the benchmark edge more than the preference signal. For a deterministic arithmetic task, either model would almost certainly produce the same answer.
